claim: Exact original DLC.DLCChecker.IsValidDLCID MethodDef 0x06001032 13-byte IL and DLC.DLCChecker.IsOwner MethodDef 0x06001033 39-byte IL are source-pinned against the matching 8,171,008-byte retail DLL. IsValidDLCID calls DLC.DLCID.GetDLCID then twice applies ceq to determine whether the returned integer is not -1. IsOwner passes this validity result into Steamworks.AppId_t constructor MemberRef then calls Steamworks.SteamApps.BIsSubscribedApp; source has a System.Object catch covering IL+15..+29 that sets return local to zero, with constructor before catch interval. Original callee MethodDef and MemberRef/type metadata, exception bytes, two leave destinations, and exact direct callers DLC.DLCManager.Update and SaveData.IsDLCInstalled are pinned. No actual installed DLC or Steam ownership outcome is established.

limits: Method and IL/source metadata prove original call and catch control flow but do not establish whether Steamworks initializes, which account is logged in, or whether BIsSubscribedApp succeeds.
The original source passes the result of IsValidDLCID into AppId_t. Do not infer that this is the mapped integer app-ID or correct an apparent surprising conversion.
The original catch System.Object covers the IL interval [15,29); it does not cover the AppId_t constructor or the validity-helper call before that interval.
DLCID.GetDLCID is pinned to an exact original 143-byte method and SHA for direct callee identity; its switch table and actual integer mapping have not been promoted as authored runtime facts here.
Direct callers are limited to two explicitly audited original functions; actual DLC ownership, installed game data, and complete calling context remain unverified.
